reviews.markdown_section:
## Code-quality review — client/

Scope: all of `client/lib` (68 files, 10,173 lines) and `client/test` (34
files, ~2,959 lines), checked against the repo's own modularity rule
(AGENTS.md: files under ~350 lines, with a dated issue owed for any chunky
file that can't be split now). Every lead was verified by opening the file;
none of the supplied leads were refuted, and two are bigger than reported.

### Formatting: no gate, and the tree isn't clean

The single most surprising result is that formatting is entirely unenforced.
`.github/workflows/ci.yml:91` runs `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos`, but
nothing checks `dart format`. Probing read-only with
`dart format --output=none lib` reports **55 of 68 files would change**.
The clearest symptom is `client/lib/api/sse.dart`: 22 tab-indented lines
(the import block at 1–4 and the whole `readProgressSse` region at 96–115)
sit inside an otherwise space-indented file — you can see the fault line at
line 116, where `readCoachSse` returns to spaces. `revisions_page.dart:52-54`
ships a mis-indented `setState` body that any formatter would fix.

This is the classic trap: the first contributor with format-on-save silently
produces a 55-file diff that buries their real work, and the tab block lives
in the SSE layer — the most timing-sensitive file in the client. The fix is
two cheap steps, worth a commit each: one behavior-neutral `dart format lib`
(verified by `flutter test`), then a `--set-exit-if-changed` step in CI.
Until that lands, every other cleanup in this review makes the eventual
format diff bigger.

### Line budget: tracked for two files, silently broken for four

The rule is real and partially working. Both heavyweight API files have
well-written split issues with target structures: `client/lib/api/client.dart`
(633 lines → core/product/stream) and `client/lib/api/models.dart`
(539 lines → four domain barrels). That is the process working as designed.

But four more files are over budget with **no issue filed**:
`features/project/project_page.dart` at 548, `l10n/en.dart` at 378,
`features/workspace/workspace_page.dart` at 371, and
`features/workspace/ideas_page.dart` at 370. A grep of `docs/issues/` for
`project_page` returns nothing. That matters most for `project_page.dart`,
which is not just long but genuinely mixed: one file holds the page build,
a leaf-evidence side-loader (`_loadLeafEvidence`, line 56), the FEAT-03
proposal decision loop and its accepted-items applier, plus three inline
dialog methods (`_edit` at 407, `_delete` at 473, `_addUpdate` at 498).
Every feature slice to the busiest screen in the app lands in this file
with no agreed seam. The two filed issues also understate current size
(~529 vs 633, ~478 vs 539), so the drift is already underway.

The l10n catalogs deserve an explicit policy rather than silence: they are
data-shaped like `models.dart`, which got an issue, so either file one or
record why key catalogs are exempt.

### Copy-paste: one FutureBuilder branch, eight homes

The pending/error branch of `FutureBuilder` is duplicated near-verbatim in
six files, all some spelling of:

```dart
Center(child: snap.hasError
    ? Text(localizedError(snap.error!, l10n.t))
    : const CircularProgressIndicator())
```

— `ideas_page.dart:125`, `settings_page.dart:63`, `revisions_page.dart:63`,
`audience_view_page.dart:70`, and twice in `roadmap_page.dart` (211, 220),
with semantic twins at `workspace_page.dart:121-123` and
`project_page.dart:143-145`. Two copies use the raw, un-localized variant —
`dashboard_page.dart:98` and `versions_page.dart:73` both render
`Text('${snap.error}')` — which is how raw exception text still reaches the
dashboard and versions screens despite `localizedError` existing as the
standard. A single shared gate widget (snapshot in, builder for data in)
deletes eight copies and fixes both leaks in one mechanical pass. This is
also the natural seam for the design pivot, which wants a different
error/empty-state treatment everywhere at once.

### Widget ownership: a theme pill living in a feature file

`ideas_page.dart:348-370` defines `ShadePill`, a pill container built from
`Cobalt` palette tokens — a theme widget by construction. Another feature
imports it: `workspace_page.dart:14` pulls in all of `ideas_page.dart` for a
single use (`ShadePill(label: l10n.t('project.quiet'))` at line 221). The
theme already owns the canonical version: `ShadeChip` in
`theme/cobalt_chip.dart:8`, with the same pill radius and a tone system.
The file also carries a single-use `extension on BorderSide { toBorder() }`
(lines 368-370) that exists only to feed line 361. One move into
`cobalt_chip.dart` (or a neutral `ShadeChip` tone covering both call sites)
plus deleting the extension removes a cross-feature import and two shapes of
the same pill before the pivot redraws them anyway.

### Smaller items, verified

- `assembly_diagram.dart:167-170`: two consecutive arms both
  `return ink` (`i == currentStep - 1` and `i < currentStep - 1`) —
  collapsible to one comparison. Dead in the strict sense: the second arm
  adds no behavior.
- `roadmap_page.dart:40-99`: one `_retryTimer` field backs both
  `_progressLoop` and `_presenceLoop`; the second `_backoff` call clobbers
  the first loop's cancel handle, and `dispose()` cancels only the latest.
  Today's behavior is correct only because abandoned timers complete their
  own completers; the twin loop bodies (56-72 vs 74-95, including the
  duplicated backoff-cap line) want one parameterized helper with per-loop
  timers.
- `step_peek.dart:220`: the landing teaser's mock git hashes are
  `['a1b2c3d', 'e4f5g6h', 'i7j8k9l']` — the latter two contain `g` through
  `l`. The first screen a visitor sees shows impossible SHAs.

### What is genuinely good

The error-localization idiom is one helper (`localizedError`,
`api/errors_l10n.dart:16`) used at 15+ sites — the duplication problem is at
least uniformly the *right* paste in most files. The test suite targets the
sharp edges rather than padding coverage: `sse_test.dart`,
`api_token_refresh_test.dart`, `errors_l10n_test.dart`, and
`leftover_scan_test.dart` — a sweep guard that fails CI if the retired
Ink & Seal tokens ever return to `lib/`. Animation and painting are kept out
of pages (`ink_motion.dart`, `assembly_diagram.dart`), and the two worst API
files already have actionable, structure-level split issues — evidence the
modularity rule has teeth when it is applied.

### Sequencing

Land the format sweep first (mechanical, unblocks review of everything
else), then the shared async-gate widget (biggest deletion count, fixes the
two raw-error leaks), then the ShadePill move, and file the
`project_page.dart` modularity issue before the next feature slice touches
that screen. The micro-cleanups (dead arms, mock hashes) ride along as one
small commit.

401s share one refresh. `sse_test.dart` (215 lines, the deepest file) covers
the SSE buffer parser, delta frames, error frames, and a five-case refresh
matrix for the coach stream. `coach_panel_test.dart` drives a finding frame
through `applyCoachFrame` and asserts both critic findings render.
`roadmap_page_test.dart`, `roadmap_presence_test.dart`, and
`roadmap_canvas_test.dart` cover the server-truth progress buckets, streamed
snapshot replacement, reconnect-after-drop, and canvas/minimap toggling.
`auth_form_magic_test.dart` covers the magic-link and code modes.
`product_dock_test.dart` covers the dock's unfinished-step routing. Token
refresh, coach SSE, roadmap canvas presence (chips), dock navigation, and
auth form modes are all mapped to real tests — this part of the advertised
behavior is genuinely covered.

The weak tier is honestly labeled: `feature_wiring_test.dart`'s own header
admits it is a "LINT-TIER BACKSTOP only … they prove presence, not behavior"
— 37 substring greps — and `leftover_scan_test.dart` greps `lib/` for retired
Ink & Seal hexes. Together they are ~2 of 34 files but they pad the count
that reads as "94 tests."

### The blind spot that mattered: chrome geometry

Both coordinator-confirmed visual defects sailed through this suite, and after
reading every test file I can say precisely why.

**Auth modal header collision** (shot 02: the cobalt dot + "InsideOut"
wordmark render above the modal card, colliding with the hero buttons). The
wordmark lives outside the card by construction — `auth_door.dart:50-70`
puts dot, wordmark, and greeting in the same Column *above* the card at
line 72. The only test that renders landing + auth is `widget_test.dart`,
which sets `Size(1200, 5000)`: at 5000px tall the centered modal is nowhere
near the hero, and `expect(find.text('InsideOut'), findsWidgets)` (line 31)
is an unbounded plural that passes with both wordmarks present.
`auth_form_magic_test.dart` pumps `AuthDoor` as the entire `home:` — the
modal over an empty page. No golden test exists anywhere in the suite (grep
for `matchesGoldenFile`: zero hits). Nothing, widget or golden, could have
failed.

**Dock overlapping the dashboard card** (shot 04: the floating pill dock
clips the chapter card's body text at 1440x900). The real shell is
`app.dart:71` `extendBody: true` plus `app.dart:135` `bottomNavigationBar:
const ProductDock()` — the body extends *behind* the dock, so every page must
reserve bottom space. `product_dock_test.dart:17` mounts the dock as a
`bottomNavigationBar` of a bare `Scaffold(body: Text(label))` with no
`extendBody` and a body that has nothing to overlap. The harness removes the
defect by construction. And there is no `dashboard_page_test.dart` at all —
the signed-in home surface is untested, including its raw error branch
(`dashboard_page.dart:98` `Text('${snap.error}')`, which violates the
documented `localizedError` standard and has no test to catch it;
`versions_page_test.dart` likewise never pumps the error branch at
`versions_page.dart:73`).

Other coverage gaps, mapped to the advertised behaviors: the presence fake
declares `onCursor` but never fires it, so roadmap cursors are untested;
profile, settings, revisions, forgot/reset/magic-link, and the export page
widget have no tests (export has only the pure-function
`export_format_test.dart`); no widget test runs in the shipped default zh-CN
locale (all hardcode `'en-US'`); and every realistic surface is exactly
1400x900 — no mobile-class viewport exists, which is a risky posture heading
into a full chrome rewrite.

Could widget/golden tests have caught the two defects? Yes, specifically:
the modal defect needs a realistic-viewport golden or a card-containment
geometry assertion (a plain widget test would not throw — the layout is a
Stack/Column, not a flex overflow); the dock defect needs an `AppScaffold`-
level test with `extendBody: true` asserting the dock rect does not intersect
visible content. Neither requires new infrastructure — only pumping what the
app actually mounts, at the size it actually runs.

### The three tests that would have caught real bugs

1. **Golden test: LandingPage + AuthDoor at 1440x900, zh-CN default, light
   and dark** — catches the confirmed wordmark-outside-the-card collision
   (and lands the pivot's zero-radius chrome with a baseline from day one).
2. **Widget test: AppScaffold with `extendBody: true` and a content-filled
   body at 1440x900, asserting the ProductDock rect does not intersect the
   last visible content rect** — catches the confirmed dock-clips-card defect
   and permanently encodes the scaffold/page bottom-padding contract the
   pivot's sticky top nav will renegotiate anyway.
3. **dashboard_page_test.dart error path: API fake throws, assert the rendered
   text resolves through the `error.*` l10n keys and `find.textContaining(
   'Exception')` finds nothing** — catches the raw `'${snap.error}'` on the
   home surface (and the identical branch in versions_page_test) and locks
   the `localizedError` standard where users actually land after login.

### Hygiene notes

`sse_test.dart:48-59` and `roadmap_presence_test.dart:39-59` are
tab-indented (mirroring the `sse.dart:96-115` drift noted elsewhere);
analyzer infos fire inside `prd_actions_test.dart`, `prd_desk_audience_test.
dart`, and `project_page_test.dart`. `cobalt_test.dart` bakes current cobalt
hexes as expectations and `leftover_scan_test.dart` greps literal hexes —
both will detonate en masse when the neo-brutalist pivot swaps the palette,
converting a design change into a red suite with no mapping from old law to
new. Rewriting those two as role-based checks (forbid raw `Color(0x` outside
the theme directory; assert geometry/role tokens instead of hexes) before
the pivot starts is the cheapest insurance in this entire report.

reviews.bottom_line: The api/session core is better than average — the single-flight refresh is correct under concurrency and loopback-tested, SSE parsing is unit-tested, the boot gate completes on error, and live-stream retries are bounded. But the client has NO timeout on any network call anywhere, which means the boot gate, the coach composer, and every data page can hang silently forever; an offline app start deletes the user's tokens; and three error surfaces either render raw English or structurally always fall through to the generic apology. All fixable with small, targeted diffs.
strengths: client/lib/api/client.dart:77-83 — single-flight refresh via `_refreshing ??= refresh().whenComplete(...)` is exactly right, and client/test/api_token_refresh_test.dart proves it against a real loopback HTTP server, including the concurrent-401 case where two simultaneous me() calls share one refresh.

client/lib/api/sse.dart:92-94 — decodeSseBytes copies chunks before running the utf8 transformer, the correct fix for multibyte characters split across web ReadableStream chunks; client/test/sse_test.dart covers the parse boundary.

client/lib/main.dart:27-34 — the boot gate lifts on error as well as success (`.then((_) => boot.complete(), onError: (_) => boot.complete())`), so a failed hydrate cannot wedge the app behind BootLoadingPage — at least when the failure is an error rather than a hang.

client/lib/features/project/roadmap_page.dart:56-95 — both live-stream loops cap backoff at 5s and treat 401/403/404 as fatal, so a deleted project or dead session does not spin the retry wheel forever.
client/lib/api/errors_l10n.dart — one mapper owns the status→localized-copy contract and is directly unit-tested; most pages route through it, which is why the two violations stand out so visibly.

findings.summary: No network call anywhere has a timeout, so a black-holed connection hangs the boot gate forever and the onError path never fires.

evidence.quote: _dio = Dio(BaseOptions(baseUrl: baseUrl, headers: {'Content-Type': 'application/json'}, validateStatus: (s) => s != null && s < 500)); — a grep for connectTimeout / receiveTimeout / sendTimeout across client/lib returns only web-font loading timeouts.

findings.failure_scenario: User on a captive-portal or packet-dropping network opens the app. hydrate()'s _me() and _refresh() never return and never throw; Future.wait never settles; boot.complete() is never called; the app sits on BootLoadingPage's spinner indefinitely with no error, no retry, and no way to reach the login form.
findings.fix: Set connectTimeout (10s) and receiveTimeout (30s) on Dio BaseOptions, and wrap hydrate's network steps in an explicit timeout so the gate lifts into the signed-out state instead of spinning.

findings.summary: hydrate() deletes stored tokens on ANY failure, so an offline or flaky app start silently logs the user out.

evidence.quote: try { user = await _me(); } catch (_) { await _refresh(); user = await _me(); } } catch (_) { user = null; await clear(); } — where clear() calls _store.delete().

findings.failure_scenario: Commuter opens the app with no connectivity. _me() fails with a transport error, _refresh() fails the same way, the outer catch runs, and both tokens are wiped from secure storage. When connectivity returns, the user must log in again — and with password-less magic-link flows that means waiting on an email. Transient network is indistinguishable from a dead session.
findings.fix: Only call clear() when the failure is an ApiException with status 401/403; on transport errors keep the token pair and leave the user signed out for this launch without deleting storage.

findings.summary: A coach SSE stream that stalls mid-response locks the composer forever — no inactivity timeout, no cancel control.

evidence.quote: enabled: !sending && retry == 0; — client/lib/api/sse_transport_web.dart:27 `final res = await web.window.fetch(url.toJS, init).toDart;` with no AbortController or deadline; client/lib/api/client.dart:502 `await readCoachSse(chunks, handlers);` waits until the connection closes.

findings.failure_scenario: The server accepts the coach POST and the LLM upstream hangs (or a proxy holds the connection open). No frames arrive, the stream never closes, `sending` stays true, and the text field plus send button are disabled with only the "thinking" hint — permanently for that panel. The user must leave the page and come back.
findings.fix: Add an inactivity timeout to sendCoach (e.g., abort if no frame arrives for 75s) using a Timer that completes/cancels the stream, and surface a localized error that unlocks the composer.

findings.summary: The coach panel stores the exception's raw English message, so its error line always renders the generic apology and its retry label is chosen by sniffing the English substring 'unavailable'.

evidence.quote: setState(() => error = e.message); — line 194 Text(localizedError(error!, l10n.t), ...) is handed a String, which matches no ApiException/DioException branch in errors_l10n.dart:16-41 and always returns `error.generic`; line 199 l10n.t(error != null && error!.contains('unavailable') ? 'coach.serviceUnavailable' : 'coach.rateLimited', ...). Server side the permit-queue 503 is "AI service is busy, try again shortly" (server/internal/agent/coach.go:150) — no 'unavailable' substring.

findings.failure_scenario: Circuit-open via the busy path (coach.go:150) shows the user "rateLimited" copy for what is actually a service outage, while any server that changes or localizes its message text silently flips the label. Meanwhile the actual error line is always the generic apology, so real failures (403, 404, 500) are indistinguishable.
findings.fix: Keep the ApiException object in state and pass it to localizedError; pick the retry label from `e.code == 'CIRCUIT_OPEN'` (or status 503), never from message text.

findings.summary: One shared _retryTimer field backs both the progress and presence backoff loops, so the second _backoff clobbers the first loop's timer handle and dispose can cancel at most one of two pending timers.

evidence.quote: _retryTimer = Timer(d, done.complete); (plain assignment, no per-loop handle); line 99 _retryTimer?.cancel(); in dispose; both loops await _backoff at lines 69 and 92.

findings.failure_scenario: Both streams drop at once (server restart). Each loop calls _backoff; the second assignment discards the first timer's reference. dispose() then cancels only the second timer; the first fires anyway, completing a completer nobody awaits — mostly harmless today only because the mounted checks catch it, but any future code that assumes dispose cancelled all timers will be wrong, and the completer garbage lingers.
findings.fix: Give each loop its own Timer local, or track timers in a set and cancel them all in dispose; keep the completer completing via `Timer(d, done.complete)` per call.

findings.summary: Live SSE streams are never cancelled when the roadmap page disposes — the web reader is never cancelled and dio gets no CancelToken — so each page visit leaks a suspended loop and an open connection until the server drops it.

evidence.quote: _readChunks loops `await reader.read()` with no `reader.cancel()` path; client/lib/api/client.dart:505-508 comment: "dio has no per-request cancel here, so the page closes by letting it die with dispose"; roadmap_page.dart:110-111 fire-and-forget loops that only exit `while (mounted)` after the current stream returns.

findings.failure_scenario: A user clicks around the roadmap, then navigates to the dashboard five times in a session. Each visit parks a progressStream/presenceStream await on a connection the server keeps open indefinitely; five suspended loops, five HTTP connections, and their setState closures live until process death or a server-side timeout.
findings.fix: Thread a cancellation signal (CancelToken for dio, a cancel callback that calls reader.cancel() for web fetch) from the page's dispose into both stream loops so the awaits unwind promptly.

findings.summary: Coach stream callbacks and catch blocks call setState with no mounted guard, so navigating away mid-stream throws setState-after-dispose.

evidence.quote: onDelta: (chunk) => setState(() => stream += chunk); — lines 96 and 99 setState(() => error = e.message) / setState(() => error = e.toString()) in catch blocks. Only the `finally` (line 101) and the fact/snack callbacks (lines 84, 90) check mounted.

findings.failure_scenario: User sends a coach message, then immediately navigates back to the PRD list while tokens are still streaming. The next delta lands in onDelta, setState runs on a disposed element, and Flutter reports an uncaught "setState() called after dispose()" async error — noise in debug, error-zone reporting in release, and a lost final chunk.
findings.fix: Guard every stream callback and catch-block setState with `if (!mounted) return;` (or the setState(() {}) pattern already used in the finally).

findings.summary: Dashboard and versions pages render the raw exception text as page content, bypassing the localizedError standard every other page follows.

evidence.quote: if (snap.hasError) return Center(child: Text('${snap.error}')); — client/lib/features/prd/versions_page.dart:73 identical line. Compare roadmap_page.dart:211/220 which use `localizedError(snap.error!, l10n.t)`.

findings.failure_scenario: A zh-CN user on the dashboard with an expired session behind a stale token sees the raw string `ApiException: invalid or expired session` (or worse, 'Request failed' from the English fallback in errors.dart:16) as the entire page body — untranslated, no retry affordance, and a broken window next to every correctly mapped page.
findings.fix: Route both branches through localizedError(snap.error!, l10n.t) and add a localized retry button that re-creates the FutureBuilder's future.

findings.summary: HTTP 5xx responses are classified as "network" errors because dio's validateStatus turns them into DioException before the mapper can read the status, making the error.server branch unreachable for normal calls.

evidence.quote: validateStatus: (s) => s != null && s < 500; — if (error is DioException || error is TimeoutException) { return t('error.network'); } — the error.server branch at lines 33-35 only triggers for ApiException, which plain HTTP 5xx never becomes.

findings.failure_scenario: The server returns 500 during a deploy. Every page tells the user a network problem on their side ("check your connection") instead of a server outage, sending them to debug Wi-Fi that was never the issue and masking real incidents from support.
findings.fix: In localizedError, inspect `DioException.response?.statusCode` before the generic DioException branch and map >=500 to error.server.

findings.summary: Web builds store both auth tokens through flutter_secure_storage, which on the web has no secure enclave and persists values in localStorage — readable by any same-origin script.

evidence.quote: _store = store ?? SecureTokenStore() with no kIsWeb branch; client/pubspec.yaml:40 `flutter_secure_storage: ^9.2.4` (web implementation degrades to localStorage; encryption is not supported there).

findings.failure_scenario: Any XSS vector (compromised dependency, injected script) reads both tokens from localStorage and impersonates the user until the refresh token rotates. Refresh rotation bounds the window but does not prevent the theft, and there is no HttpOnly-cookie alternative in the current architecture.
findings.direction: Accept and document the web trade-off with refresh-token rotation as the mitigation and short access-token TTL, or move web sessions to an HttpOnly cookie + SameSite=Lax model.
findings.first_check: Confirm the deployed threat model treats XSS as out of scope or not (docs/architecture/), then record the decision where token storage is documented.

findings.summary: The TimeoutException branch of localizedError is untestable in production because nothing in the client can throw one — there are no timeouts anywhere.

evidence.quote: if (error is DioException || error is TimeoutException); client/test/errors_l10n_test.dart:33 `expect(key(TimeoutException('t')), 'error.network');` — no timeout configuration exists in client/lib.

findings.failure_scenario: The test suite green-lights a timeout contract the runtime cannot deliver; a future reader assumes hangs are already handled and skips adding real timeouts (the REL-01 gap).
findings.fix: Land REL-01's timeouts (which make Dio throw TimeoutException), keeping this branch and its test honest; until then note the branch is aspirational.

findings.summary: Brightness is detected by comparing the resolved surface color to a constant instead of asking the theme, an identity check that breaks the moment any theme variant reuses the same ground color.

evidence.quote: extension on Cobalt { bool get brightnessIsDark => surfaceBase == Cobalt.darkGround; }

findings.failure_scenario: A high-contrast or "pure black" dark variant (or the incoming neo-brutalist four-step ladder) that uses a different dark ground hex, or a light theme that happens to share the constant, flips every coach panel ink/field decision to the wrong polarity.
findings.fix: Use `Theme.of(context).brightness` (or pass Brightness down from the build method) instead of comparing colors.

recommendations: Set explicit Dio timeouts — connectTimeout 10s, receiveTimeout 30s — in ApiClient's BaseOptions, and wrap Session.hydrate's network steps in a 15s timeout so the boot gate always lifts.
In Session.hydrate, only clear stored tokens on ApiException 401/403; on transport failures keep the token pair and present a signed-out state for this launch without deleting storage.
Add a frame-inactivity timeout (about 75s) and a cancel path to sendCoach so a stalled coach stream releases the composer instead of locking it.
Store the ApiException object in CoachPanel state, pass it to localizedError, and derive the retry label from e.code/status rather than English message substrings.
Give each roadmap retry loop its own Timer handle and thread cancellation (dio CancelToken, web reader.cancel()) into progressStream and presenceStream so dispose actually tears the streams down.
Route dashboard_page.dart:98 and versions_page.dart:73 through localizedError and give both pages a localized retry action.
Map DioException carrying a >=500 response status to error.server in localizedError so server outages stop masquerading as user network failures.
Add mounted guards to CoachPanel's onDelta and catch-block setState calls, and record the web localStorage token-storage trade-off in the architecture docs with rotation as the stated mitigation.
reviews.next_first: Set two limits before the next run: a 10s connect / 30s receive timeout on Dio (plus a 15s hydrate timeout) so nothing can hang the boot gate, and a 75-second coach-stream inactivity timeout so a stalled SSE response cannot lock the composer.
reviews.markdown_section:
## Reliability & ops review — frontend

**Scope.** `client/lib/api` (client.dart, sse.dart, sse_transport_web.dart,
errors.dart, errors_l10n.dart), `client/lib/session` (token_store.dart,
session.dart, boot.dart), `features/prd/coach_panel.dart`,
`features/project/roadmap_page.dart`, and the error surfaces on
dashboard_page.dart and versions_page.dart. The question this pass asks: if
the network misbehaves, does the client degrade predictably — and the
honest answer is "sometimes, and the worst cases are the silent ones."

### What is genuinely solid

The auth-recovery core is the strongest part of the client. The refresh
interceptor in `client/lib/api/client.dart:47-71` correctly handles the
subtle parts: `/auth/*` 401s are terminal and untouched, the retry marker
in `options.extra` prevents loops, a failed refresh clears the session so
the router lands on the auth door, and `_refreshSingleFlight` (lines 77-83)
collapses a thundering herd of simultaneous 401s into one refresh. This is
not just plausible on paper — `client/test/api_token_refresh_test.dart`
exercises it against a real loopback HTTP server, including the
concurrent-requests case asserting exactly one refresh POST. The web-side
mirror in `coachSseWithRefresh` (sse.dart:167-190) re-applies the same
policy to the raw fetch path that bypasses dio, including clearing tokens
after a failed refresh so the user is not trapped in a "stream failed"
loop.

The SSE layer is likewise careful: `decodeSseBytes` (sse.dart:92-94)
copies each chunk before running the UTF-8 transformer, which is the
correct treatment for multibyte characters split across ReadableStream
chunks, and `parseSseBuffer` leaves partial frames in the carry buffer.
The server's writers (e.g. `server/internal/api/presence_routes.go:103`,
`roadmap_progress.go:64`) all emit LF-terminated `event:/data:` frames, so
the splitter matches the wire format in practice. The boot gate
(`main.dart:27-34`) completes on error as well as success, and the
roadmap retry loops are properly bounded — 500ms doubling to a 5s cap —
with 401/403/404 treated as fatal so a dead session does not spin.

### The big hole: there is no timeout anywhere

`BaseOptions` in client.dart:30-34 sets baseUrl, a content-type header,
and `validateStatus` — and no `connectTimeout`, `receiveTimeout`, or
`sendTimeout`. A grep across `client/lib` confirms the only
`Duration(seconds:)` timeouts in the tree belong to web-font loading and
UI countdown timers. This turns "the network is weird" from an error into
a disappearance, in three places:

1. **The boot gate can hang forever.** `Session.hydrate()` calls `_me()`
   and, on failure, `_refresh()` — both unbounded. `main.dart`'s
   `Future.wait(...).then(..., onError: boot.complete)` handles *errors*,
   but a black-holed connection (captive portal, firewall DROP rule) is
   neither resolution nor rejection. The app sits on `BootLoadingPage`
   indefinitely; the only escape is a reload on a better network.
2. **The coach composer can lock forever.** If the server accepts the
   coach POST and the upstream hangs mid-stream, no frames arrive, the
   fetch never settles, `sending` stays true, and the text field stays
   disabled (`coach_panel.dart:212`) with no cancel control.
3. **Every data page spinner can spin forever.** All the FutureBuilder
   pages await dio futures with no ceiling.

Tellingly, `errors_l10n.dart:38` has a `TimeoutException` branch and
`errors_l10n_test.dart:33` asserts it — a tested contract the runtime
cannot currently produce. The first limit to set before the next run is a
10s connect / 30s receive timeout on Dio, plus a ~15s timeout around
hydrate's network steps so the gate always lifts into a defined state.

### hydrate() conflates "offline" with "logged out"

`session.dart:52-60` nests `_me()` → `_refresh()` → re-`_me()`, and the
outer `catch (_) { user = null; await clear(); }` deletes both tokens for
*any* exception — a 401, but also a `SocketException` on a commuter train.
The result: an offline app start silently wipes the session, and the user
re-authenticates (magic-link email and all) for what was a dead tunnel,
not a dead session. The fix is a one-line distinction: clear storage only
for ApiException with status 401/403; treat transport errors as
"signed out for this launch" without touching the store.

### Error surfaces: three ways to be wrong

The dashboard and versions pages render `'${snap.error}'` directly
(dashboard_page.dart:98, versions_page.dart:73) — raw English exception
text as the entire page body in a zh-CN-first product, with no retry
button, while roadmap_page routes through `localizedError` correctly. The
coach panel has the opposite, subtler bug: it stores `e.message` (a
String), then hands that string to `localizedError` (coach_panel.dart:194),
which matches no typed branch and *always* returns `error.generic` — the
real failure classification is discarded before it reaches the UI. Worse,
the countdown label at line 199 is chosen by sniffing the English
substring `'unavailable'`, and the server's permit-queue 503 says "AI
service is busy, try again shortly" (`server/internal/agent/coach.go:150`)
— so a circuit event is labeled "rate limited". Store the exception, not
its message; branch on `code`/`status`, never on text.

One more classification wrinkle: `validateStatus: s < 500` means ordinary
HTTP 5xx arrives as a `DioException`, which the mapper reports as
"network" — so during a server deploy every page blames the user's
connection, and the `error.server` branch is unreachable for plain HTTP
calls. Checking `DioException.response?.statusCode` first fixes it.

### Lifecycle leaks on the roadmap page

Two findings compound here. First, the single `_retryTimer` field
(roadmap_page.dart:40) backs both backoff loops: `_backoff` assigns it
(line 45), so the second loop's timer clobbers the first loop's handle,
and `dispose` cancels at most one of two pending timers. The mounted
checks make this mostly harmless today, but it is exactly the kind of
shared-mutable-handle bug that bites the next edit. Second, and more
materially, the live streams are never actually cancelled: the web reader
loop (`sse_transport_web.dart:35-44`) has no `reader.cancel()` path, the
dio side has no CancelToken (the client.dart:505-508 comment admits the
page "closes by letting it die with dispose"), and the progress/presence
loops only re-check `mounted` after the current stream returns — which,
for a healthy connection, is never. Every roadmap visit parks suspended
loops and open connections until the server or the process dies.

The coach panel has the matching lifecycle bug in callback form:
`onDelta` (coach_panel.dart:80) and both catch blocks (lines 96, 99) call
`setState` with no `mounted` guard, so navigating away mid-stream throws
setState-after-dispose. The sibling callbacks got the guard; these three
did not.

### Token storage and the pivot

On web — the primary documented target — `SecureTokenStore` is just
flutter_secure_storage, whose web backend is localStorage with no secure
enclave and no encryption: any same-origin script can read both tokens.
Refresh-token rotation bounds the exposure window but does not remove it;
this is a documented-the-web-trade-off or move-to-HttpOnly-cookie
decision, not a code bug, but it should be written down in the
architecture docs rather than left implicit.

None of this blocks the neo-brutalist pivot, but one reviewed line does
intersect it: `brightnessIsDark` is computed by comparing the resolved
surface color to `Cobalt.darkGround` (coach_panel.dart:230-232) rather
than asking the theme. A four-step near-black ladder with more than one
dark ground hex will silently flip coach-panel polarity. Ask
`Theme.of(context).brightness` while you are already touching the file for
the timeout work.

### Priority order

1. REL-01: dio timeouts + hydrate timeout (lifts the boot-gate hang).
2. REL-02: stop clearing tokens on transport errors.
3. REL-03: coach-stream inactivity timeout + cancel.
4. REL-04/REL-08: exception-object error state; localizedError everywhere.
5. REL-05/REL-06/REL-07: per-loop timers and real stream cancellation.

The two limits to set before the next run: **10s connect / 30s receive on
Dio (with a 15s hydrate ceiling)** and **a 75s coach-stream inactivity
timeout**. Both are small diffs against well-tested seams.

reviews.bottom_line: Endpoint inventory is complete — every dock item and page action traces to a real ApiClient method, and the API_BASE env contract is coherent across code, docs, and Dockerfile. But the client ships a systemic silent-failure pattern on every primary write action (no try/catch, no SnackBar, no reload on error) and the bottom dock — the app's main navigation — can route to the wrong workspace's project and bounces to the dashboard after a refresh. Both are squarely fullstack defects on documented paths, plus a file-size-rule gap the repo's own contract says must be filed.
strengths: client/lib/api/client.dart — token refresh is architecturally sound: single-flight refresh (lines 77-83), a /auth/* carve-out so terminal 401s surface untouched (lines 51-56), and resolve-retry inside onResponse (lines 66-70). This is the hard part of an API client done right.

reviews.markdown_section:
## Fullstack review — client behavior, endpoint coverage, and env contract

Scope: `client/lib/router.dart`, all feature pages at action level, `api/client.dart`
+ `api/requests.dart`, `chrome/product_dock.dart` + `chrome/loop_focus.dart`, the
`main.dart` → `app.dart` boot chain, `pubspec.yaml`, and
`docs/usage/local-development.md`. I traced every named control: the six dock items,
idea capture and convert-to-PRD, the commit dialog, the export download path,
invite-code join, and the admin signup-mode toggle. Verdict: the API surface is
complete and the configuration contract is honest, but the client has a systemic
silent-failure pattern on write actions and a dock that sometimes navigates to the
wrong project.

### What checks out

**Endpoint coverage is complete.** Every affordance I traced maps to a real
`ApiClient` method: dock items resolve to `/workspace/:id/ideas`, `/prd/:id`,
`/prd/:id/versions`, `/projects/:id/roadmap`, and the project page (the Evidence
surface); idea capture → `createIdea`, convert → `convertIdea` (which returns the
new `prdId` and navigates to it); commit dialog → `commitPrd` with the readiness
carry list; export → `exportPrd` with format/audience query params; join →
`joinWorkspace`; admin → `setSignupMode`/`createInvitation`/`revokeInvitation`. I
found no place where the UI asks for something the client cannot send. The
reference-design "UI asks, API never sends" hole does not exist here.

**The env contract is coherent.** `session/session.dart:7-10` reads
`String.fromEnvironment('API_BASE', defaultValue: 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/v1')`;
`local-development.md:45,121` documents the identical `--dart-define`; the
Dockerfile bakes `ARG API_BASE=/api/v1` for same-origin nginx. Code, docs, and
deploy agree.

**Token refresh is the best code in the client.** Single-flight refresh, a `/auth/*`
carve-out so bad credentials surface untouched, and interceptor-level resolve-retry
(`api/client.dart:47-83`). The SSE paths even re-read the rotated token on retry.
The admin signup-mode toggle works end to end and re-reads its state after writing.

### What fails

**Every primary write action can fail silently (FULL-01, High).** The pattern
repeats across the loop's spine: `ideas_page._captureNow`, idea convert,
`versions_page._commitDialog`, dashboard create/join, `prd_page._save`, repo
save/sync on the project page — all `await api.…` inside button callbacks with no
try/catch. A 409, 422, or dropped connection produces an unhandled async error in
the logs and *nothing* on screen: no SnackBar, and `_reload()` never runs. The
worst instance is the version commit: the user taps 提交版本, the server rejects the
commit, and the UI offers no evidence either way. `project_page._decide` already
demonstrates the correct pattern (catch → `localizedError` → SnackBar); the fix is
to extract it once and apply it everywhere.

**The dock can open the wrong workspace's project (FULL-02, High).** `ProductDock._go`
resolves the project as `focus.projectId ?? _projectOnRoute(context)`
(product_dock.dart:91), and `IdeasPage._seedProject` early-returns whenever any
projectId is already set (ideas_page.dart:38) — nothing clears or re-keys it when
the user crosses workspaces. From workspace B's ideas wall, dock "Roadmap" routes
to workspace A's roadmap. The dock is the product's primary navigation; a
navigation control that crosses workspace boundaries on a labeled button fails the
"does each button do what it says" test outright.

**The dock's step memory is boot-scoped (FULL-03, Medium).** `LoopFocus` is a fresh
`ChangeNotifierProvider` per boot (main.dart:41) with no persistence and no
path-parameter seeding on the PRD pages. Refresh `/prd/:id` and the dock correctly
highlights 版本 — then tapping it falls through `stay()` to `/dashboard`, because
`focus.prdId` is null and `_projectOnRoute` only matches `/projects/`. The
highlighted button ejects the user from the page it represents. Relatedly, 记下 and
想法 are two dock buttons with one identical destination, and the dashboard's
"Capture idea" silently chooses `list.first` of the user's workspaces.

**Export polish (FULL-04/FULL-05).** The markdown download branch discards the
stub's documented false return while the print branch beside it handles the same
contract — on the shipped iOS/Android targets the Download button is a silent
no-op. The page's primary action is also labeled `common.save` ("Save") for what is
really "generate a preview," which misstates the action.

Smaller items: the audience view issues eight identical `getPrd` calls per load
(FULL-06); three feature files are over the ~350-line rule with no dated modularity
issue filed — `project_page.dart` at 548 is the largest file in the client after
the two already-filed API files (FULL-07); the commit dialog closes silently on an
empty name (FULL-08); the project page headlines itself "Evidence" while loading
(FULL-09); and a failed readiness fetch before commit discards the carry list
(FULL-10).

### Pivot note

The reference shell is a sticky top-nav with *no bottom nav*; today's chrome is a
floating bottom dock that the coordinator confirmed visually clips page content
(and my look at `shots/11-versions-dark.png` shows the dock parked on top of the
commit card's gap list at 1440×900). Killing the dock in the pivot retires FULL-02
and FULL-03 wholesale — the strongest argument for taking the reference layout
literally rather than restyling the dock. Nothing else in these findings is
design-coupled: the guarded-action helper, the export fallback, and the audience
view fetch hoist survive the re-skin unchanged.

### Cheapest user-visible fix

One shared guarded-action wrapper, applied to the six unguarded write actions
first: idea capture, convert, version commit, workspace join/create, and PRD save.
It is roughly sixty lines, needs no design input, and converts an entire class of
silent failures into translated, visible feedback on the exact paths the product
demo walks.

reviews.bottom_line: The advertised web feature set is overwhelmingly real and traceable to code: all sixteen checked features are IMPLEMENTED or PARTIAL, none are DEAD or DOCS-ONLY at the page level. The core loop (capture → convert → coach → PRD desk → roadmap → commit → export) has a working implementation for every step. What separates this from a clean bill is the last mile of each feature: the idea wall's primary one-line capture path renders a raw English status enum, evidence display silently empties on any failure and covers only 5 done leaves against a README promise of automatic attach, audience pickers leak raw enum English into the zh-CN UI, the coach's critic findings drop severity and never clear, and Material chrome stays English because MaterialApp never receives a locale. All fixable in small diffs before the neo-brutalist pivot.
strengths: Coach SSE is fully wired end-to-end with frame-level handling for delta, prd_updated, stage_changed, fact_recorded, and critic_findings, plus eager 401-refresh semantics (client/lib/api/sse.dart:116-148, 167-190).

The Progress view is rendered from server truth (GET /roadmap/progress and a live SSE stream) with Now / needsDeadline / Next / Done lanes and pressure coloring, matching PRODUCT.md's time-first default (client/lib/features/project/roadmap_progress_view.dart:15-53, client/lib/features/project/roadmap_page.dart:56-72).

The human Commit surface is complete: audience-scoped readiness with gaps, carry-into-commit of unresolved items, diff counts, and a fanned stack visualization (client/lib/features/prd/versions_page.dart:44-65, client/lib/features/prd/versions_stack.dart:150-201).

Presence and remote cursors are genuinely live: dual SSE loops with capped backoff, throttled cursor writes (200ms), self-cursor filtering, and dead-session cleanup (client/lib/features/project/roadmap_page.dart:49-95, client/lib/features/project/roadmap_canvas.dart:83-107).

Auth breadth is real: password, magic-link (with token-consuming landing page), 6-digit code with resend, forgot/reset, and invite-code prefill driven by the public signup-mode config (client/lib/features/auth/auth_form.dart:11, 77-107, client/lib/features/auth/magic_link_page.dart:30-37).

reviews.markdown_section:
# Feature implementation review — frontend vs. README/PRODUCT claims

This review checked every frontend-facing claim in `README.md` and `PRODUCT.md` against the
implementing code in `client/lib`, and checked the live screenshots under
`docs/review/2026-10-06-frontend-cobalt/shots/` where useful. Verdict first: the advertised
feature set is real. Every one of the sixteen checked features is IMPLEMENTED or PARTIAL at
the page level; nothing advertised is DEAD or DOCS-ONLY. The gaps are in the last mile of
otherwise-working features, and nearly all are small diffs.

## Feature matrix

| Advertised feature (README / PRODUCT.md) | Verdict | Implementing code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Idea inbox capture | IMPLEMENTED | `ideas_page.dart:60-66,195-224` (screenshot 08 confirms) |
| Idea type wall | IMPLEMENTED | `ideas_page.dart:233-249` — flat responsive `Wrap` of posters |
| Convert idea to PRD | IMPLEMENTED (no error handling) | `ideas_page.dart:133-140` → `/prd/:id` |
| AI coach conversation over SSE (stages, suggestions, critic findings) | IMPLEMENTED | `api/sse.dart:116-148` handles all five frame types; `coach_panel.dart:147-150,171-190` |
| PRD desk editing + eight sections | IMPLEMENTED | `prd_desk.dart:87-111`; exactly 8 keys in `models.dart:251-260` |
| Roadmap canvas with presence + remote cursors | IMPLEMENTED | `roadmap_page.dart:56-95,193-203`; `roadmap_canvas.dart:83-107` |
| Now / Next / Later bands | IMPLEMENTED | `roadmap_bands.dart:38-86` |
| Time-first Progress view with deadlines/pressure | IMPLEMENTED | `roadmap_progress_view.dart:15-53`, fed by server truth + SSE; deadline editing in `roadmap_node_card.dart:203-224` |
| Human Commit + versions stack + readiness | IMPLEMENTED | `versions_page.dart:44-65`; `versions_stack.dart:150-201` (readiness gaps, diff counts, carry-into-commit) |
| Audience views (decision / management / delivery / validation) | PARTIAL | `audience_view_page.dart` — functional, but raw English enum chips at line 55 |
| PRD export (markdown / print) | IMPLEMENTED | `export_page.dart:49-99` — markdown download + print-HTML-to-tab with fallback |
| Evidence attach + GitHub sync display | PARTIAL | `project_page.dart:191-287` — manual sync, done-leaves only, cap 5, silent failure |
| Workspace invitations + member roles | IMPLEMENTED | `settings_page.dart:101-131`; join-by-code at `dashboard_page.dart:56-75` |
| Admin signup-mode + invitation ledger | IMPLEMENTED | `admin_section.dart:38-67,139-148,169-197` (three modes, used/revoked states, revoke) |
| Dark mode | IMPLEMENTED | `appearance.dart:46,67-71`; light/dark themes wired at `app.dart:22-23,40` |
| zh-CN / en-US locale switch | IMPLEMENTED (with Material-locale caveat) | `appearance.dart:61-65`; `app.dart:100-104`; but no `locale:` on MaterialApp |
| Magic-link / code / password auth | IMPLEMENTED | `auth_form.dart:11,77-107`; `magic_link_page.dart:30-37`; forgot/reset pages present |

## What works and is worth protecting

The coaching pipeline is the deepest implementation in the client and the hardest to get
right: `readCoachSse` parses multibyte-safe SSE frames and dispatches `delta`,
`prd_updated`, `stage_changed`, `fact_recorded`, and `critic_findings` to typed handlers
(`api/sse.dart:116-148`), with an eager 401-refresh wrapper that mirrors the dio interceptor
policy for the raw-fetch web path (`sse.dart:167-190`). The PRD desk reflects streamed
section updates back into the section controllers (`prd_page.dart:179-186`). The roadmap
runs two independent SSE loops (progress + presence) with capped exponential backoff and a
200ms-throttled cursor write, and the canvas renders labeled remote pointers with dead-session
cleanup. The Commit flow honors the "human authority stays explicit" principle in PRODUCT.md:
the dialog carries unresolved readiness gaps into the commit, the stack renders per-audience
readiness with blocking gaps called out, and nothing auto-commits. These are the features the
neo-brutalist pivot must not break.

## Where the implementation falls short of the advertisement

**The idea wall's primary path shows a raw English enum.** Quick capture always stores empty
content (`ideas_page.dart:63`), and the poster body falls back to `idea.status` verbatim
(`ideas_page.dart:326`) — so every one-line idea, the README's very first web-loop step,
displays "inbox" instead of 收集箱 even though the localized key exists (`zh.dart:35`). The
same two paths (`_captureNow`, `onConvert`) have no try/catch: a failed capture or convert is
a silent no-op on the highest-traffic screen, while `project_page.dart:86-101` demonstrates
the correct `localizedError` snackbar pattern two features away.

**Evidence over-promises and under-delivers.** README.md:18-19 says commits, PRs, and
deployments "attach themselves to roadmap nodes as evidence". The web client offers a manual
立即同步 button, displays evidence only for up to five done leaf nodes
(`project_page.dart:63` `.take(5)`), and swallows every failure into an empty page
(`project_page.dart:72-74`). On the page whose entire pitch is "progress you can verify,
not claims you have to trust", a failed token or a sixth done item is indistinguishable from
"GitHub binding is broken". There is also no human attach/correct affordance, which the
evidence trust layer in PRODUCT.md:184-195 ("small actions to confirm, correct, remove, or
discuss") will eventually require.

**zh-CN leaks.** The audience switcher on the reader-view page and the export dropdown render
raw `Text(a)` enum labels (`audience_view_page.dart:55`, `export_page.dart:67`) while the
versions page right next door localizes the same four values correctly
(`versions_stack.dart:47`). Worse, neither `MaterialApp` receives `locale:` or
`supportedLocales:` (`app.dart:28-42`), so the deadline date picker — on the documented
deadline-setting path — renders English month names and CANCEL/OK to a zh-first user, and
`admin_section.dart:103` hardcodes an always-English close button via a
`MaterialLocalizationsNo` workaround instead of fixing the root cause.

**The coach's error and critique contracts are partial.** The panel flattens `ApiException`
to `e.message` before calling `localizedError` (`coach_panel.dart:95-99`), which only
handles exception objects — so a 429 becomes a generic apology — and then distinguishes
"service unavailable" from "rate limited" by sniffing the English substring "unavailable"
(line 199). The fact-recorded snackbar interpolates a raw `Map` (line 86). Critic findings
render only the issue string under a raw 'critic' label, discarding the severity and
recommendation fields the frame carries, and the list is never cleared, so findings from an
earlier stage shadow later conversation (lines 89-93, 188-190). PRODUCT.md:139-141 promises a
severity-ranked overview handled individually; the UI currently shows an unranked, immortal
quote list.

**Bands fallback contradicts Now semantics.** When server progress truth is absent,
`RoadmapBands.bucket` files `done` work into the Now band (`roadmap_bands.dart:38-44`),
which is exactly what PRODUCT.md:53-54 says cannot be: done work is not Now work. The
Progress tab agrees with the server; the Bands tab, briefly, does not.

**Smaller but visible.** Project updates render raw RFC3339 timestamps (`project_page.dart:307`;
screenshot 07 confirms "2026-10-06T00:31:05+08:00") in a codebase that ships `timeAgo` and
`isoDate`. The versions and dashboard pages render raw exception text as whole-page content
(`versions_page.dart:73`, `dashboard_page.dart:98`), bypassing the `localizedError` standard
the other pages follow. The landing canvas — the product's evidence-pitch storefront — shows
fake commit hashes containing non-hex characters ('e4f5g6h', 'i7j8k9l',
`step_peek.dart:220`) and a dead duplicated branch (`assembly_diagram.dart:167-170`). And
`ideas_page.dart` carries its own `ShadePill` (lines 348-366) duplicating the shared
`cobalt_chip.dart` `ShadeChip`, which means the incoming neo-brutalist pivot would migrate
chips twice unless this is collapsed first.

## Features to stop advertising until fixed

1. **README.md:18-19 — "commits, PRs, and deployments attach themselves to roadmap nodes as
   evidence"**: the web client is manual-sync-only, shows at most five done leaves, and
   silently empties on failure. Reword to "sync on demand" (or ship auto-sync plus a real
   evidence surface) before the next release notes repeat the claim.
2. **PRODUCT.md:138-141 critique handling ("severity-ranked overview … recommendation and a
   keep-as-is option")**: the frontend renders issue text only, unranked and un-clearable.
   Either scope this as target-only explicitly or land the severity rendering; as written it
   reads like shipped behavior.
3. **The idea-privacy hint (`idea.privateHint`, visible in screenshot 08: "仅自己可见——想法默认
   只有作者能看到")**: the frontend cannot enforce or verify this — it depends entirely on
   server-side filtering of `listIdeas`. Keep the copy only if a test proves a non-author,
   non-admin member cannot see another author's inbox ideas; otherwise soften the hint.

Everything else advertised — the eight-section PRD desk, coach streaming with stages,
presence and cursors, Now/Next/Later plus the server-truth Progress view, the human Commit
with readiness, audience projections, markdown/print export, invitations and the admin
ledger, dark mode, the locale switch, and all three auth ways — is implemented and safe to
keep advertising. The recommended order is to fix the ideas-wall pair first (FEAT-01/02),
since that is the first screen of the advertised loop, then the evidence surface, then the
zh-CN leaks, and to fold the component dedup (FEAT-12) into the pre-pivot checklist so the
neo-brutalist migration touches each component exactly once.

reviews.bottom_line: The stranger path from clone to running frontend now holds, the design docs and tokens agree on most of the lock, and CI genuinely guards the client — but the two most-seen surfaces of the product (the signed-in navigation dock and the first-touch auth modal) render visibly broken at a common laptop viewport, the written design law and the code have drifted apart in a half-dozen small places, an unexplained pubspec.lock downgrade is sitting uncommitted, and the incoming neo-brutalist pivot has no plan row, no design-qa thread, and no token seam prepared for it.
strengths: The README quick start is finally coherent end-to-end: env.sh init → dev.sh migrate/run → `cd client && flutter run -d chrome` (README.md:79-99), the client's default API_BASE is the local server (client/lib/session/session.dart:7-10 `defaultValue: 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/v1'`), and invitation-only signup is documented with the bootstrap path (README.md:132-137).

The records culture this repo demands is mostly real: two prior whole-tree reviews with skeptic passes and reproduction tables, a design-qa log that preserves verbatim user quotes and their resolutions, and a plan board that already reflects the f185e94 simulation fixes (docs/plans/README.md:12-13).

## PM review — frontend Cobalt, main @ f185e94

**Bottom line: 6.0/10.** A stranger can finally get from clone to a running
frontend, the design law and the token file agree on the spine, and CI truly
guards the client — but the two surfaces every user sees first are visibly
broken at a common laptop viewport, the law and the code have drifted in a
half-dozen quiet places, an unexplained dependency downgrade is sitting in
the worktree, and the neo-brutalist pivot the user wants next has no plan,
no record, and no prepared seam in the tokens.

### Can a stranger follow the README from clone to a running frontend?

Yes — and this is a real recovery from review 1, where the quick start
dead-ended three separate ways. Today's README (README.md:79-99) walks
`env.sh init` → `dev.sh migrate` → `dev.sh run` → `cd client && flutter run -d chrome`,
states plainly that `dev.sh` is not optional, and documents the
invitation-only default with its bootstrap (`promote-admin`, mint invites)
at README.md:132-137. The client defaults its API base to the local server
(`client/lib/session/session.dart:7-10`), so the README's bare `flutter run`
command actually works; the CORS trap review 1 filed (FS-03) is closed because
`dev.sh` now exports `INSIDEOUT_CORS_ORIGINS=localhost` for client runs
(docs/usage/local-development.md:124-127). Two gaps remain: no user-facing
document pins the Flutter version ("Flutter 3" is the entire guidance,
local-development.md:11, while CI and `client/Dockerfile` pin 3.44.0), and
the worktree's dirty `client/pubspec.lock` — which *downgrades* intl, matcher,
meta, test_api, and vector_math — is exactly what a version-unpinned
`flutter pub get` produces. That lockfile must be restored or deliberately
re-committed, and the version must be written down where strangers look.

### Does DESIGN.md's lock match cobalt.dart and the pages?

Mostly — and the agreement is worth saying precisely, because it is what the
pivot will lean on. All seven locked hexes appear verbatim in
`client/lib/theme/cobalt.dart:62-70`; the button lock ("14px 24px", cobalt
fill) matches `cobalt_theme.dart:62-69`; the type lock (Display 48–58, Title
26+, Body 17.5, Meta 12) matches `cobalt_theme.dart:129-145`; cards are 20px
radius with a cobalt-200 hairline; chips are shade pills, not chops
(`client/lib/theme/cobalt_chip.dart`). The drift is at the edges, and it is
all one-directional (code exceeds or contradicts the law): the dashboard
Home numeral is an ad-hoc 120px (`dashboard_page.dart:204`) against the
48–58 Display band DESIGN.md assigns to "page names and the Home numeral";
`cobalt.dart` defines `radiusControl = 12.0` against the `control: 9999px`
pill decree (used once, in `step_peek.dart:148`, where it is not a control);
and the dock — which DESIGN.md mandates as "bottom dock… no Linear-style left
rail" — currently renders at the *vertical center* of the viewport on every
signed-in page, because `AppScaffold` combines `extendBody: true` with a
`bottomNavigationBar` whose child `Center` expands into the full-height slot
(app.dart:71,135; product_dock.dart:28), while the bounding constant
`ProductDock.height = 88.0` sits unused two screens up from where it is
needed. The screenshots in `docs/review/2026-10-06-frontend-cobalt/shots/`
confirm it on dashboard (chapter-card body clipped), workspace (the dock
covers 「删除这个工作区」), and roadmap (empty state bisected). The auth modal
has the complementary problem: its cobalt dot, "InsideOut" wordmark, and
greeting are Column *siblings above* the card (`auth_door.dart:50-70`), so
over the `black54` barrier they collide with the landing hero and both CTAs
— shot 02 shows the wordmark sitting on top of 「开始打磨」. DESIGN.md's "cards
on a field" law is one surface; the modal draws two.

### What did prior reviews already file?

This review must not re-file, and does not: USER-01 (invitation-only
undocumented — now in README), FS-02/FS-03 (invite deep link, CORS — closed
in the remediation waves), USER-02/USER-10 (token refresh — see the
`api_token_refresh_test` the client now ships), FEAT-01/FEAT-02 (quiet flag
and board — review-2 wave 3 code), the raw-English-error cluster (the
`localizedError` mapper exists; residual call sites belong to the code
reviewers), the band-widget duplication (review-2 code-quality), the
client.dart/models.dart line-budget issues (filed 2026-09-18 / 2026-10-04),
and review-2's PM features-left ledger (Branch/Merge, Decision Log,
per-project authority — explicitly end-state and parked by design). What is
*new* here: the two chrome-level rendering Highs (PM-01, PM-02), the
lock/code drift pair (PM-05, PM-06), the lockfile churn (PM-03), the
unpinned toolchain (PM-04), the missing pivot records (PM-07), the hardcoded
paint at the pivot's first surfaces (PM-08), CI's blind spot for layout
(PM-09), and three small record-hygiene items (PM-10, PM-11, PM-12) —
HANDOFF's stale "worktree is clean", DESIGN.md's absence from every index,
and the three over-budget feature files with no modularity issue.

### CI and worktree hygiene

The client CI job (ci.yml:72-95) is genuinely good: pinned Flutter 3.44.0 in
lockstep with the shipped image, analyze with infos as the accepted baseline,
the full test suite, and a release web build. Its blind spot is total for
this bug class: both confirmed Highs compile, analyze, and unit-test green.
A golden or headless-screenshot smoke on the shell and AuthDoor is the
cheapest insurance the pivot will ever buy. The worktree itself is a mixed
picture: the docs/plans and HANDOFF modifications are the honest in-flight
record of f185e94 and should be committed as their own checkpoint, but
`client/pubspec.lock` does not belong in that commit, and HANDOFF's
"worktree is clean" sentence (still present at line 126) is exactly the
warning the file exists to carry. The untracked
`docs/review/2026-10-06-frontend-cobalt/` folder also needs its index README
per `docs/review/README.md` convention.

### How the current design complicates the pivot

The incoming language is the current one's photographic negative: radius
impossible by decree versus a 999px pill law; 2px borders on everything
versus hairline-only cards; hard offset shadows versus soft elevation; a
top-nav h-16 shell versus the bottom dock that is currently misrendering;
a four-step background ladder versus blur shadows. Two structural facts
matter for sequencing. First, the good news: the Cobalt token class is a
single 28-field seam, so a pivot can land as token + theme changes first and
page sweeps second — but only after the hardcoded paint at landing_page,
auth_door, and product_dock is pulled into tokens, or the first screen will
be half-pivoted. Second, the record obligation: PRODUCT.md:438-443 codifies
Cobalt as the brand commitment and the design-qa log's newest entry is
2026-09-18; the 2026-08-19 thread ("an infra migration does not mean visual
change") is the precedent for what happens when a visual change proceeds
without a recorded decision. The pivot needs its dated plan, its board row,
its design-qa thread with the cobalt-palette variant of the brief, and its
DESIGN.md amendment — before the first radius is zeroed. And it should
inherit a fixed dock and a single-surface auth modal first, or it will be
debugging layout on two fires at once

reviews.markdown_section:
## First-Run User Review

I walked the new-user path in order against the capture set in `docs/review/2026-10-06-frontend-cobalt/shots/` — landing (01), login modal (02), register modal (03), dashboard light/dark (04/05), then workspace (06/12), project (07/13), ideas wall (08/14), PRD desk (09/15), roadmap (10/16), versions (11/17), profile (18), plus the narrow shots (19/20) — and read the code behind each beat: `landing_page.dart`, `auth_door.dart`, `auth_form.dart`, `dashboard_page.dart`, `app.dart`, `product_dock.dart`, `workspace_page.dart`, `project_page.dart`, `ideas_page.dart`, `prd_desk.dart`, `coach_panel.dart`, `versions_stack.dart`, and the zh/en catalogs. I scored the first three minutes **4/10**.

**What works.** The landing page is the best part of the funnel. The hero ("把想法，一件件打磨出来。") plus one sentence of subtitle tells a new visitor exactly what InsideOut does — capture ideas, let an AI coach grind them into a PRD, split them into a parallel roadmap, and track real commits to delivery — and the four-step assembly story below reinforces it (`landing_page.dart:14-19`). The register modal states the password rule inline. The ideas wall is the strongest in-product surface: the capture input is the visual focus, and the privacy caption ("仅自己可见——想法默认只有作者能看到…") is precisely the reassurance a first-time user needs before typing an unpolished thought. Light and dark themes are coherent across every paired shot, zh/en catalogs are at parity, and the versions page's per-audience readiness checklist is a genuinely good piece of product design. The roadmap empty state tells you what to do next.

**Where it breaks.** The first failure is the chrome. The floating dock renders at the *vertical center* of every signed-in screen, not the bottom: the dashboard chapter paragraph is clipped mid-sentence (04/05), the workspace delete row is half-hidden (06/12), and the versions checklist's last two items are unreadable (11/17). The cause is in `product_dock.dart:26-29`: the widget returns `SafeArea(child: Center(...))` and `AppScaffold` (app.dart:135) inserts it as `Scaffold.bottomNavigationBar` — a `Center` expands to fill the loose height the Scaffold offers, so the nav bar silently becomes full-height and the pill centers in it. The intended `static const height = 88.0` exists but is never referenced. This one bug also explains why the workspace page's create-project FAB (its only creation affordance, `workspace_page.dart:115-118`) is nowhere in shots 06/12: the FAB anchors relative to a nav bar whose top is at the viewport top. A new user in a fresh workspace quite literally cannot start a project.

The dock also teaches unreliability. `DockItem.evidence` unconditionally calls `stay()` (product_dock.dart:129-130) — a labeled navigation button that is a guaranteed no-op with no toast, no disabled state. `DockItem.version` navigates to `/prd/$prd`, which is the page already open when you're on the desk — another silent dead click (captures.md A6). On top of that, the "unfinished" nudge replaces the 提交 label with the longer "未完成：提交", which overflows its slot and lands as a white pill on the icon (10/18) — designed behavior that reads as a stuck tooltip.

Information architecture adds friction. The project page headlines itself "证据" in the largest type, with the actual project name demoted beneath (`project_page.dart:150-155`), so a user who clicked "Onboarding Revamp" can't confirm where they are. The workspace page is four label-only rows — 想法 / 设置 / 编辑 / 删除这个工作区 — with no chevron and no description, and the destructive row is styled identically to the neutral ones (A7); FieldCard has no trailing affordance at all. The dashboard hides "create workspace" once you have one (the button only exists in the empty state, `dashboard_page.dart:231-247`). The auth modal card itself is untitled: the disc, "InsideOut", and the "登录/创建账号" greeting are siblings *above* the card in a centered Column (`auth_door.dart:50-71`), which is why the wordmark floats over the landing hero and collides with the 开始打磨/登录 buttons in shot 02 (the lead reviewer's confirmed defect) — and even when it doesn't collide, the greeting is 12px bodySmall dark text on a black54 scrim.

Data surfaces feel half-finished. The updates feed shows a raw English enum chip ("progress") and a raw ISO timestamp (`project_page.dart:304-307`) while the workspace card two screens away renders "进展 · 8 小时前" from the same data — the l10n keys exist. The PRD desk shows three big section cards with no body, no placeholder, and borderless fields (`prd_desk.dart:96-107`), so the first-run user has no idea the coach's questions are meant to be answered there. The versions readiness list mixes languages on one line: localized section name + raw server English gloss (`versions_stack.dart:184`). Smaller wobbles: clicking an idea card's title or body does nothing (only the tiny PRD chip works); the invite banner's hint ends in a dangling colon; "大段引语" renders as a permanent subtitle under the coach title with nothing beneath it; the cryptic manifesto line "没有标签，也没有文件夹。" floats centered below the only idea card.

**What I would do first.** Fix the dock layout: bound `bottomNavigationBar` to the already-defined 88px height and bottom-align the pill. That single change clears the content overlap on every screen, restores the create-project FAB, and makes the existing per-page bottom padding actually meaningful. Immediately after, wire the two silent dock dead clicks and the idea-card tap, re-run the sim walk in `scripts/sim`, and only then take the copy/IA pass (project heading, dashboard labels, destructive-row styling). The bones of a trustworthy product are visible on the landing page and ideas wall; the chrome between them is currently spending that trust faster than the screens earn it back.

reviews.bottom_line: The current UI is a coherent, well-disciplined execution of the *rounded* Cobalt card lock — and that is precisely the problem: against the Cobalt-Neo target it fails all four structural pillars. There is no shadow system at all (elevation is explicitly zeroed and the only two shadows in the app are soft Material blurs), every radius token (12/20/28/999) is the exact inverse of the 0px decree, container borders are 1px periwinkle hairlines instead of 2px, and no press-the-block interaction or 100ms motion token exists anywhere. The cobalt palette itself is faithfully and cleanly tokenized, and dark/light parity is real — so the migration is a token-layer rebuild, not a rewrite. Score 2.5/10 against the Cobalt-Neo target.

True dark/light parity from a single class: cobalt.dart:102-154 mirrors every semantic key; shots 05-dashboard-dark and 09-prd-desk-dark render consistently with their light twins 04/15.
